Compare Cross-Validated Prediction Scores

Source: R/cv_comparison.R
cv_tab.Rd

Rank candidate models by one held-out score, after checking that every candidate was scored on the same folds and the same observations. Lower scores are better.

Usage

cv_tab(mod_list, metric, by_fold = FALSE)

Arguments

mod_list

Named list of complete cross-validation results to compare, for example list(landscape = cv, null = null_cv). The names label the rows of the table and must be unique. Every candidate must use identical folds, responses, trials, and frequency weights, and the candidates must be of compatible kinds (see "What can be compared").

metric

One score name, chosen explicitly: "rmse", "mae", "neg_log_score", "deviance", or "brier". Every candidate must have recorded it. There is no default, because the scores answer different questions.

by_fold

Logical. The default FALSE ranks the pooled scores. TRUE ranks the candidates separately within each fold, which shows whether a ranking is consistent across folds.

Value

A data frame with one row per candidate (per candidate and fold when by_fold = TRUE), sorted from best to worst. Its columns are:

  • Modnames: the candidate's name in mod_list.

  • Rank: 1 for the best score. Tied scores share the lowest rank.

  • Score: the pooled score, or the fold score when by_fold = TRUE.

  • Delta: Score minus the best score, in the units of the score. It is NA when every score is infinite.

  • Metric, Unit: the score and what one score refers to, for example "observation", "trial", or "choice_set". See multiScaleR_cv.

  • N_assessment, N_scored, Weight_sum: the planned assessment occurrences, the number that entered the score, and their total weight.

  • Warnings: the number of warnings recorded while fitting the candidate (in that fold when by_fold = TRUE). Read them in the candidate's warnings element.

  • Fold: the fold, when by_fold = TRUE.

The candidate results themselves are not modified.

How to read the table

The best candidate is listed first. Delta is each candidate's distance from it, in the units of the score. For RMSE and MAE that is a difference in response units, such as animals per survey. For the negative log score, a Delta of D means the best model gave the observed outcomes exp(D) times the probability, as a geometric mean per observation (per choice set for conditional choice). The per-fold table from by_fold = TRUE is descriptive. Use it to see whether one fold drives a ranking, never to pick a model for that fold from its own assessment score.

What can be compared

Every candidate must be complete, with no failed fold. An incomplete candidate stops the comparison, because a model scored only on its easier folds would look better than it is. No failed model or fold is removed silently. Results of different kinds cannot be mixed.

ResultsComparisons allowed
Gaussian, Poisson, and binomial from cross_validate() and cross_validate_glm()RMSE and MAE across families on identical observations. The log score, deviance, and Brier score need the same family and link.
NB2 or Gamma, alone or with Gaussian or PoissonRMSE and MAE across these families on identical observations. Log scores between Poisson and NB2 on the same counts. A Gamma log score compares only with another Gamma.
cross_validate_clogit()Other conditional-choice results with the same complete sets and partial-likelihood method, using neg_log_score only.
cross_validate_field()Other field results with the same responses, folds, and projected coordinates. Poisson and NB2 share a count target.
cross_validate_mixed()Other mixed-model results with the same groups, prediction target, and folds.
cross_validate_bayes()Other Bayesian results with the same targets, folds, and blocks, using neg_log_score only.

A binomial log score refers to the probability of the observed count of successes, while a Brier score is a mean over individual trials. Field, mixed-model, and Bayesian log scores are joint scores for blocks of held-out observations, so they are kept apart from the per-observation scores of ordinary GLMs.

What the table does not do

The scores carry no penalty for model complexity, and Delta is not an AIC difference, an Akaike weight, or a model probability. The spread of fold scores is not a standard error, because folds share training data and are few. If you use the table to choose a model or a tuning rule, the winning score is optimistic. Evaluate that choice with an independent test set or an outer validation layer. To score a predeclared rule that picks a model by training AIC, AICc, or BIC, use select_cv().

See also

cross_validate(), cross_validate_glm(), select_cv(), multiScaleR_cv, aic_tab(), and vignette("v08-cross-validation", package = "multiScaleR").

Examples

data("landscape_counts")
data("surv_pts")
# Three spatial folds. The simulated coordinates are in meters.
folds <- spatial_cv_folds(crds(vect(surv_pts)), block_size = 1000, k = 3,
                          crs = 32617)
candidates <- list(
  null = cross_validate_glm(counts ~ 1, landscape_counts, folds,
                            family = "poisson"),
  site = cross_validate_glm(counts ~ site, landscape_counts, folds,
                            family = "poisson"))

# Pooled ranking. Delta is the gap from the best model in animals per survey.
cv_tab(candidates, metric = "rmse")
#>   Modnames Rank    Score      Delta Metric        Unit N_assessment N_scored
#> 1     null    1 2.210604 0.00000000   rmse observation          100      100
#> 2     site    2 2.232857 0.02225306   rmse observation          100      100
#>   Weight_sum Warnings
#> 1        100        0
#> 2        100        0

# exp(Delta) is how many times more probability the best model gave the
# observed counts, as a geometric mean per survey
cv_tab(candidates, metric = "neg_log_score")
#>   Modnames Rank    Score       Delta        Metric        Unit N_assessment
#> 1     null    1 2.163750 0.000000000 neg_log_score observation          100
#> 2     site    2 2.169778 0.006027989 neg_log_score observation          100
#>   N_scored Weight_sum Warnings
#> 1      100        100        0
#> 2      100        100        0

# Is the ranking the same in every fold?
cv_tab(candidates, metric = "rmse", by_fold = TRUE)
#>   Modnames Rank    Score       Delta Metric        Unit N_assessment N_scored
#> 1     null    1 2.017854 0.000000000   rmse observation           34       34
#> 2     site    2 2.091114 0.073260576   rmse observation           34       34
#> 3     null    1 1.608284 0.000000000   rmse observation           33       33
#> 4     site    2 1.620645 0.012360460   rmse observation           33       33
#> 5     site    1 2.824229 0.000000000   rmse observation           33       33
#> 6     null    2 2.833142 0.008912299   rmse observation           33       33
#>   Weight_sum Warnings  Fold
#> 1         34        0 fold1
#> 2         34        0 fold1
#> 3         33        0 fold2
#> 4         33        0 fold2
#> 5         33        0 fold3
#> 6         33        0 fold3
